messages.author: dc00a99e2f28f20f
messages.subject: identifying phrases within a text
parts:
Hello,

I'm looking for some code that will produce output of three or four
word phrases in a text.

Quantitative Corpus (pages 120-124) generates word pairs and my
attempt at using the RWeka Ngram tokenizer generated an error message
(simple_triplet_matrix' -probably related to the sparse matrix though
I am seeking advice on this).

I'd be interested to know if anyone has done something similar or
code recommendations.

Any assistance is appreciated.

Regards

Bob

messages.author: 3957c1a92561c3c1
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] identifying phrases within a text

I'm not sure if that is what you are looking for, but you could use the openNLP package (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/openNLP/openNLP.pdf) to parse your text and then extract the phrases.
It's just an idea though.

Best wishes,
Martin

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] identifying phrases within a text
parts:
> I'm looking for some code that will produce output of three or four word phrases in a text. Quantitative Corpus (pages 120-124) generates word pairs [...]
And that code can be extended for n-grams. I even thought I had an
assignment or exercise in the book that did that ... maybe not. Here's
what I use (not pretty, not fast, but usually works):

word.grammy <- function (vector, gramlength, sep = " ", output = 1:2)
{
if (length(vector) < gramlength) {
return(NA)
break
}
out1 <- apply(mapply(seq, 1:(length(vector) - gramlength +
1), gramlength:length(vector)), 2, function(q) paste(vector[q],
collapse = sep))
out2 <- sort(table(out1), decreasing = T)
list.output <- list(`element-wise ngrams` = out1, summary = out2)
return(list.output[output])
}

# as in
qwe <- c("qgq3gvqe vrgvqegvgqe rgveqg eqgeqrgvqe geqrgveqgveq
geqrgveqr gveqgeqrv gtqegqergveq rgveqrgvqergv gqrevgqre gvqegqergve
gqrgeg qegqegqegqegqe gqerq ergvgeqrgvq egrqegeqr gvqvrgqgqervgeqrg
qerrgqvrgqer")
asd <- unlist(strsplit(qwe, " "))
word.grammy(asd, 3, " ", output=1)

Best,
STG
